c.tagline: Morocco's relaxed ocean capital of kasbahs, gardens and storks.

taxi.fareNote: Rabat's blue petits taxis are metered and cheap for up to three passengers within the city, so insist on the meter (compteur). Careem also operates via app, and beige grands taxis run fixed shared intercity routes.

emergency.note: Dial 19 for police in cities, 15 for medical/SAMU, and 177 for the Gendarmerie Royale outside urban areas.

avoid.reason: No true no-go areas; at most avoid deserted medina lanes and the beach/corniche late at night.
Mind pickpockets in the medina, at Rabat-Ville station and in market crowds, and politely decline unofficial 'guides'.

hood_desc: Rabat's walled old town, gentler and more orderly than those of Fes or Marrakech, with a straight souk street of textiles and crafts running down toward the ocean and the Kasbah of the Udayas at its northern edge; atmospheric riads and easy sightseeing.

The monumental government quarter of grand boulevards, home to the Hassan Tower and the Mausoleum of Mohammed V, close to the tram and train station; a central, dignified base within walking distance of the medina.
Rabat's fashionable modern district of tree-lined avenues, cafes, bars, boutiques and restaurants popular with students and young professionals; the city's go-to area for dining and nightlife.
The French-built new town of orderly Art Deco boulevards centred on Avenue Mohammed V, with hotels, offices and the main train station; a convenient, walkable heart of the modern city.
A leafy, upscale residential suburb of villas, embassies and luxury hotels south of the centre; calm, green and exclusive, better for a quiet stay than for being in the thick of things.

water.note: City tap water is treated and generally safe, though many visitors prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: The tramway runs roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM (later on weekends); buses cover similar hours with reduced late-night service.
transit.note: The modern Rabat-Sale tramway has two lines (L1 and L2) linking Rabat with Sale across the Bouregreg, complemented by an Alsa-run city bus and trambus network; petits taxis fill in for door-to-door trips.
transit.pay: Tram tickets (around 7 MAD) are bought from platform machines and validated on board; a single ticket allows intermodal transfer to Bus Line 30. Taxis and buses are paid in cash.

transit.m: City bus toward central Rabat (~30-40 min)
Petit/grand taxi to the city center (15-20 min, ~150 MAD fixed)

tip.r: Customary; leave ~10% at restaurants, round up taxi fares and tip cafe waiters a few dirhams.
